Dies gilt auch für Bewerber, denen keine Information über die Ablehnung ihrer Bewerbung zur Verfügung gestellt wurde, bevor die Mitteilung über die Zuschlagsentscheidung an die betroffenen Bieter ergangen ist. Eine gleichlautende Bestimmung ist in § 62 Abs. 2 VgV jedoch auf Verlangen des Bewerbers/Bieters enthalten. Nach § 39 VgV wird spätestens 30 Tage nach Zuschlagserteilung eine Vergabebekanntmachung mit den Ergebnissen des Vergabeverfahrens über den Datenservice des Bundes an das Amt für Veröffentlichungen der Europäischen Union übermittelt. Hierin wir der Name des erfolgreichen Bieters sowie die Nationalität des wirtschaftlichen Eigentümers des Unternehmens, sofern es nicht börsennotiert ist, veröffentlicht. Recht auf Auskunft, Berichtigung, Löschung, Einschränkung der Verarbeitung personenbezogener Daten Diese Rechte ergeben sich aus den Artikeln 15 bis 18 DSGVO i. V. m. §§ 12-14 DSG NRW. Recht auf Auskunft Es besteht ein Recht auf Auskunft der von der Vergabestelle verarbeiteten personenbezogenen Daten. Recht auf Berichtigung: Es besteht ein Recht auf Berichtigung, sofern die den Bewerber/Bieter betreffenden Angaben nicht (mehr) zutreffend sind. Unvollständige Daten können vervollständigt werden. Recht auf Löschung Es besteht grundsätzlich ein Recht auf Löschung der personenbezogenen Daten. Der Anspruch hängt jedoch u. a. davon ab, ob die Daten zur Erfüllung der Aufgaben noch benötigt werden (s. a. Dauer der Speicherung). Recht auf Einschränkung der Verarbeitung Es besteht ein Recht, eine Einschränkung der Verarbeitung der Daten des Bewerbers/Bieters zu verlangen, sofern nicht ein wichtiges öffentliches Interesse dem entgegensteht (z. Der Auftragnehmer muss darüber hinaus: • über Erfahrung in der strukturierten Erbringung von Betriebs-, Support- und Projektleistungen verfügen, • in der Lage sein, komplexe Anforderungen verständlich zu analysieren und umzusetzen, • über etablierte interne Prozesse zur Qualitätssicherung verfügen, • eine transparente Kommunikation und Dokumentation sicherstellen, • einen Wissenstransfer innerhalb des Projekt- und Betriebsteams gewährleis- ten, • sicherstellen, dass Personalwechsel die Leistungserbringung nicht wesentlich beeinträchtigen. Nachweise sind beizufügen, z. It will draw them in and build on the knowledge and skill acquired in each stage. Programme Aim The purpose of this training programme is to design, develop and deliver a training programme that build people’s understanding of self-harm and the role it plays in the life of a person who self-harms. The programme will build the knowledge and confidence of the learner to have a conversation if they are concerned that someone may be self-harming. The training programme should provide people who access it with a sense of hope and reassurance that people can build healthier coping mechanisms. Programme Objectives The training programme is intended to: Increase understanding of what self-harm is. Increase understanding of the relationship between self-harm and suicide. Build skills and confidence to engage with a person and speak openly about self-harm. Challenge the stigma surrounding self-harm Increase awareness of available supports and services Stage 1: An introduction to the subject of self-harm – communicating the ‘why’ functions of self-harm through lived experience experts. The training programme will actively support the work of the Sláintecare Healthy Communities Programme building the capacity of workers and volunteers across the Healthy Communities network working to promote and improve the health and wellbeing of people living in the community areas. 4. Tender Description 4.1 Tender deliverables – In Scope The HSE seeks to award a Contract to a Single Source Supplier for the provision of an Online Training Programme – Understanding Self-Harm. The successful provider will be required to design, develop and deliver an interactive online training programme titled, ‘Understanding Self-Harm’ for members of the public, with an emphasis on action learning outcomes. The content material for the online programme will be written and prepared by an expert project group chaired by the HSE NOSP. Statement of Work paragraph 2.1 requires documented evidence of past performance migrating legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365 and the Power Platform. Two questions on this paragraph: a. Is 2.1 a pass or fail responsibility requirement, or is it evaluated as part of the past performance factor described in the evaluation criteria? b. Where an offeror's relevant past performance was performed under commercial contracts rather than federal prime contracts, will the Government accept that commercial past performance? Will the Government also accept the relevant past performance of proposed key personnel or of a proposed subcontractor? Answer: Paragraph 2.1 is evaluated as part of the Government’s technical assessment of the offeror’s relevant past performance and technical competency, rather than as a separate pass/fail responsibility determination. The Government will accept relevant commercial past performance, not just federal prime contract experience, provided the quoted experience demonstrates comparable scope, complexity, and relevance to the requirement. The Government may also consider relevant experience of proposed key personnel and proposed subcontractors, to the extent the quote clearly identifies the experience, exp

any required interim milestones or target dates within the 180-calendar-day period for architecture/design approval, development, UAT, production migration, and final handoff? Answer: Timeline requirements for individual deliverables/CLINs are amended as follows: Deliverable D.1 required within 45 days of contract award. Deliverables D.2 through D.8 required within 160 days of contract award. Deliverables D.9 through D.10 required within 180 days of contract award. 63. Section G requires certification documentation for Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online. May the offeror satisfy this requirement with certifications held by named key personnel who will perform the work, or must the certifications be held at the offeror entity level? Answer: The Government will accept certifications held by the individual personnel proposed to perform the work. An organizational-level Microsoft designation or partner status is not required to satisfy this certification requirement. 64. Will the contractor receive a dedicated development/sandbox site collection or Power Platform environment within the Government’s Flank Speed tenant before detailed design (D.1), or is all build work to occur in a contractor-owned tenant with export/import packaging for Government deployment? If teaming is permissible, please also advise whether there is a preferred format for identifying each team member's qualifications, roles, and past performance within the quotation. The First Alert Advanced platform represents a critical technological evolution that introduces proprietary Agentic AI capabilities essential to the Government's mission. Government software that relies entirely on proprietary data feeds, closed-source algorithms, and intellectual property owned exclusively by the OEM. No other commercial vendor has the legal right or technical capability to access the existing Government infrastructure, modify the current software instances, or integrate the proprietary "Advanced" agentic AI modules. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 calendar days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. A sole source Justification & Approval document is currently being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is to procure annual software licenses and support for Dataminr’s First Alert Advanced (P/N: DM-FAFC-ADV-IND), a proprietary, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) real-time, AI-powered intelligence platform. This new Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract will upgrade the Government's existing First Alert licensing posture into a single, unified vehicle, while expanding capacity to support new requirements for additional Government partners. The contract structure includes a 12-month Base Year and four (4) 12-month Option Years. The Government is seeking 50 base First Alert Advanced individual use licenses with up to 21 optional licenses to support joint Government operations. The First Alert Advanced platform represents a critical technological evolution that introduces proprietary Agentic AI capabilities essential to the Government's mission. These capabilities include Tactical Predictive Intelligence, which leverages Dataminr’s proprietary

AI methods—ranging from statistical event modeling to deep learning and machine learning—to detect anomalies in this time-series data, alerting watch-standers to critical national security events such as aircraft diverting from scheduled routes or exhibiting unexpected shifts in altitude or course. At this time, the incumbent contractor and original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Dataminr, Inc., is the only source capable of providing all necessary services. The requirement constitutes a highly specialized upgrade of existing, integrated Government software that relies entirely on proprietary data feeds, closed-source algorithms, and intellectual property owned exclusively by the OEM. Dataminr, Inc. maintains no authorized resellers or distributors. No other commercial vendor has the legal right or technical capability to access the existing Government infrastructure, modify the current software instances, or integrate the proprietary "Advanced" agentic AI modules. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 cal

n and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 518210 (Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services) will be used for determining company size status. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. This service is also extended to eligible American citizens residing abroad. It is a globally integrated system serving over 9.6 million beneficiaries, including active-duty service members, retirees, and their families. The MHS is unique in that it functions as both a direct healthcare provider and a multi-billion-dollar health insurance payer through the TRICARE program. Its ultimate success

e medical capabilities, austere mission environments, field hospitals and Forward Operating Bases. DoW’s close relationship with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is paramount. The success of an integrated Federal Electronic Health Record (EHR) is a top national priority. Equally critical is the ability to support the continuum of care across operational and enterprise healthcare environments, ensuring that health information generated during military operations can be captured, exchanged, and made available to support continued care within the enterprise health record.
